sentenceSets.sentence: The heinous nature of the crime made it impossible to discuss dispassionately in any public forum.

answerChoices.reasoning: The sentence says the crime could not be discussed 'dispassionately,' implying strong moral condemnation, not mere controversy or debate.
The sentence emphasizes moral outrage that disrupted calm discussion; 'egregious' means flagrantly bad but lacks the specific connotation of shocking evil.
'Reprehensible' means deserving blame, but the sentence stresses that the crime was impossible to treat dispassionately, suggesting a deeper kind of moral horror.
'Atrocious' is very close but emphasizes cruelty more than shock; the sentence frames the crime as something that triggers visceral emotional reaction in public discussion.
The sentence says the crime could not be discussed calmly in any forum, indicating something far worse than merely unfortunate or regrettable.
Whether the crime was illegal is not what the sentence is conveying; it focuses on the moral character that made calm public discussion impossible.
The sentence attributes the difficulty of public discussion to the moral character of the crime, not to its complexity or nuance.
'Tragic' implies sorrow and loss, but the sentence's emphasis on the impossibility of dispassionate discussion points to moral horror, not sadness.
The sentence describes something that provoked strong emotional reactions preventing calm discussion, not something that was merely strange or odd.
Something mundane would not make public discussion impossible; the sentence clearly describes something that provoked intense moral outrage.
The sentence conveys clear moral condemnation so strong it prevented dispassionate discussion; ambiguity would not produce this effect.

sentenceSets.sentence: The tribunal was convened specifically to address the most heinous violations, those so extreme that ordinary courts had declined jurisdiction.

answerChoices.reasoning: The sentence distinguishes these violations by their extreme moral character—courts declined jurisdiction—not by how many people they affected.
'Flagrant' means openly scandalous, but the sentence specifies violations so extreme ordinary courts stepped aside, implying moral horror beyond mere obviousness.
The sentence explains courts declined jurisdiction because of the character of the violations, not because of their organized or methodical nature.
'Indefensible' focuses on the impossibility of justification; the sentence focuses on violations so shocking that ordinary courts declined to handle them.
The sentence describes violations extreme enough that ordinary courts stepped aside entirely—'serious' is far too mild to capture that level of severity.
All violations before a tribunal would be unlawful; the sentence distinguishes these as uniquely extreme, not just illegal.
Whether violations were documented is irrelevant to why the sentence was convened; the sentence emphasizes the extreme moral nature of the offenses.
The sentence does not frame these violations as political; it describes them as extreme enough that ordinary courts declined jurisdiction.
The sentence explains the tribunal was needed because of the extreme character of the violations, not because of when they occurred.
The sentence attributes the exceptional nature of these violations to their extreme moral character, not to any technical or procedural complexity.
The sentence explicitly contrasts these violations with what ordinary courts could handle, indicating they were extraordinarily severe, not minor.

sentenceSets.sentence: Even those who had long advocated leniency in sentencing recoiled at the heinous details that emerged during the trial.

answerChoices.reasoning: 'Disturbing' captures discomfort but not the moral shock; the sentence specifies that even advocates of leniency recoiled, suggesting something shockingly evil.
'Graphic' describes vividness of presentation, but the sentence says even leniency advocates recoiled, pointing to the moral character of what was revealed, not its explicitness.
'Damning' implies evidence that proves guilt, but the sentence's emphasis on recoiling by leniency advocates points to moral horror, not legal incrimination.
'Horrifying' is close but broader; the sentence specifically frames the reaction as a reversal by leniency advocates, pointing to something that crossed a moral threshold.
The sentence attributes the recoiling of leniency advocates to the moral character of the details, not to their unexpectedness.
The sentence focuses on the moral reaction of observers, not on whether the details proved legal guilt.
'Sensational' implies media dramatization; the sentence describes genuine moral recoil even among those predisposed to leniency.
The sentence does not suggest the details were numerous or extensive; it focuses on their morally shocking character.
Details that caused even leniency advocates to recoil could not be boring; the sentence clearly describes something profoundly disturbing.
The sentence describes details extraordinary enough to reverse the position of committed leniency advocates—the opposite of routine.
The sentence describes details that caused recoiling; encouraging details would produce the opposite reaction.
